function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – Quick Reference Guide** | Topic | Key Points | Where to Find More Info | |-------|------------|------------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits apply unless otherwise indicated.
• 55 mph on rural interstates, 65 mph on urban interstates.
• 45 mph on rural highways, 55 mph on urban highways.
• 35 mph on rural roads with 2‑lane or 4‑lane highways.
• 25 mph on residential streets (unless posted otherwise). | Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT) – Speed Limits page | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑seat Requirements** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• Children under 4 must be in a rear‑facing seat. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | TxDOT – Cell Phone Use | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21 (0.02% BAC).
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | Texas Alcoholic Beverage Commission (TABC) – DUI | | **Right‑of‑Way Rules** | • Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks.
• Stop at stop signs and yield at yield signs.
• In a four‑way stop, the first vehicle to arrive has the right of way. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **School‑Bus Rules** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children.
• No passing on either side of a stopped school bus. | TxDOT – School Bus Safety | | **Lane‑Changing & Passing** | • Use turn signals.
• Do not pass on the right unless the vehicle ahead is turning left. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Headlights & Lighting** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise, and during rain, fog, or low visibility. | TxDOT – Headlights | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking in front of driveways, fire hydrants, or on sidewalks.
• No parking in a “no parking” zone or on a “no stopping” zone. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • All vehicles must be registered and display a valid license plate.
• Most vehicles must pass an annual safety inspection. | Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV) | | **Traffic Cameras & Automated Enforcement** | • Cameras enforce speed limits, red‑light violations, and other infractions. | TxDOT – Automated Enforcement | | **Special Vehicle Rules** | • Bicyclists must ride in the lane if possible; otherwise, they may use the shoulder.
• Motorcycles must obey the same rules as cars but may use the shoulder. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Emergency Vehicles** | • Drivers must yield to emergency vehicles with flashing lights or sirens. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Roadside Assistance & Tow Rules** | • Tow trucks must have a valid license and insurance.
• Roadside assistance must be performed safely and legally. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | --- ### How to Get Official, Up‑to‑Date Information 1. **Texas Transportation Code** – The primary source for all traffic laws. *Website:* https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/Docs/TX/htm/TX.545.htm 2. **TxDOT Traffic Safety** – Offers educational materials, statistics, and updates. *Website:* https://www.txdot.gov/traffic-safety.html 3. **TxDMV** – For registration, licensing, and inspection requirements. *Website:* https://www.txdmv.gov/ 4. **TABC** – For DUI laws and enforcement. *Website:* https://www.tabc.state.tx.us/ 5. **Local County or City Ordinances** – Some municipalities have additional rules (e.g., parking restrictions, speed limits in business districts). Check your local city or county website. --- ### Quick Tips for Safe Driving in Texas - **Always keep your headlights on** during low‑visibility conditions. - **Use your turn signals** well before changing lanes or turning. - **Never drive under the influence** – the penalties are severe. - **Respect school‑bus rules** – stopping is mandatory. - **Check your vehicle’s registration and inspection status** before hitting the road. - **Stay alert for traffic cameras** – they enforce speed limits and red‑light violations. --- **Need More Specific Information?** If you’re looking for details on a particular rule (e.g., “What are the exact penalties for a 0.09% BAC?” or “How does Texas handle hit‑and‑run cases?”), let me know and I can dive deeper or pull up the relevant statutes.
